fields.title: What does multimodal alignment align: vectors, visual interfaces, or evidence dependence?
fields.thesis: CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 produce comparable vectors. BLIP-2 and LLaVA connect vision to conditional generation, CV-OPD trains visual evidence use, and UMRM scores responses. Their supervision and interfaces differ, not a single capability ladder.
fields.axis_0: Retrieval vectors, visual tokens, generated responses, or rewards
fields.axis_1: Dual towers, connectors, policy distributions, or heads on frozen features
fields.axis_2: Paired similarity, instruction labels, view contrasts, or perturbation preferences
fields.axis_3: Visual sequence length, embedding width, teacher, and scorer costs

fields.position: Independent image and text encoders map to the unit sphere with symmetric in-batch contrastive loss.
fields.tradeoff: Category text can be a zero-shot prototype, but similarity is not open answers. Local clothing retrieval does not reproduce 400M image-text pretraining.

fields.position: Q-Former extracts visual features with a fixed set of learned cross-attention queries and feeds a frozen LLM.
fields.tradeoff: The trainable bottleneck limits visual sequence length and can miss detail. Four local queries do not reproduce full two-stage training.

fields.position: Project vision into the language-token space and learn conditional responses with multimodal instructions.
fields.tradeoff: Shape alignment is not semantic or instruction alignment. A local lightweight QA head does not generate GPT-4 instruction data or train LLaVA-13B.

fields.position: Independent modality towers produce shared 768-dimensional vectors; MRL supports specified prefix truncation followed by renormalization.
fields.tradeoff: Narrower embeddings and fewer visual inputs are distinct budgets. Official local checkpoint validation covers text and images, not all four modalities.

fields.position: The student reads the full image; positive and negative teachers differ only in crop and share the student prefix. JSD and CDL constrain evidence use.
fields.tradeoff: Negative crops and sample/token gates shape supervision. Local evidence includes actual VLM L1 updates and A100 diagnostics, not complete visual capability.

fields.position: Freeze VLM hidden states, pool only the response, and train a bias-free reward head on caption perturbation preferences.
fields.tradeoff: No human preferences does not mean no labels: layer selection and a bootstrap verifier use supervision. Local reward accuracy does not ensure policy-selection utility.

fields.title: A shared retrieval space is not a language input space
fields.body: CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 align vector similarities; the latter supports selected MRL dimensions. BLIP-2 queries and LLaVA projections condition an LLM and require generative training to use them. Matching dimensions or retrieval semantics do not make a vector a general-purpose visual soft prompt.

fields.title: A good-looking answer and genuine image evidence use differ
fields.body: UMRM learns rewards from caption perturbations and checks selection of policy-generated responses, rather than only hand-built negatives. CV-OPD changes teacher crops under a fixed student prefix to constrain distributions directly. Evaluation and distillation can complement each other without a reward benchmark proving visual attribution.

fields.title: October 29: publication update and evidence boundary
fields.body: The formal EmbeddingGemma 2 paper is the October 6 model, not a new identity. It describes pooling 512-dimensional backbone features then projecting to 768. Pinned official code projects before returning `last_hidden_state`; equal-weight masked means commute with that linear map. Keep the 16-image GPU result at its prior evidence grade, not audio/video or seven-benchmark acceptance.

fields.question: Why doesn't correct image retrieval with CLIP or EmbeddingGemma 2 show LLaVA can answer image questions?
fields.answer: Retrieval matches candidate representations. LLaVA generates answer tokens from an image, question, and context, which needs a generative interface and supervision. Compare the same output task, not retrieval hits pooled with answer correctness.
fields.example: Retrieving an image of cups does not establish counting them, citing evidence, or following an answer format.

fields.question: Do fewer BLIP-2 queries and narrower EmbeddingGemma 2 vectors save the same resource?
fields.answer: Q-Former queries determine visual sequence length to the LLM. MRL width affects retrieval-vector storage and similarity. Both can lose information but at different stages; use trained prefixes with renormalization, not coordinate deletion as visual pooling.
fields.example: Thirty-two visual tokens and a 256-dimensional vector are length and width, not directly comparable.

fields.question: Does UMRM detecting a caption color perturbation show the CV-OPD student uses the right image region?
fields.answer: UMRM ranks one negative distribution, while policy errors can differ. CV-OPD compares student and positive/negative crop teachers on a shared prefix. Correct judging, receiving that training signal, and genuinely changing evidence use are separate checks.
fields.example: A judge spotting red changed to blue does not show the student stopped guessing common colors.

fields.question: When can prior results survive a difference between paper and code operator order?
fields.answer: Check the actual operations. The same bias-free linear projection commutes with equal-weight masked averaging and the pinned code/checkpoint did not change. Nonlinearity, different weights, or retraining do not inherit equivalence. Only provenance changes here.
fields.example: `mean(W h1,W h2)=W mean(h1,h2)`; averaging two GELU outputs generally does not equal GELU of their mean.

fields.summary: Initial version: compared CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 retrieval, BLIP-2/LLaVA interfaces, CV-OPD evidence use, and UMRM rewards; screened 20 abstracts and read six papers closely.

The formal EmbeddingGemma 2 paper describes the October 6 model, so no duplicate identity is added. It pools 512-dimensional features before projection to 768; pinned code projects before `last_hidden_state`, equivalent under equal-weight masked averaging. The prior 16-image GPU run does not qualify audio, video, or seven full benchmarks.
